stories.title: EU staking review threatens crypto yields and network security
stories.summary: The European Union is reviewing rules for crypto staking, CryptoSlate reports. The review could change how staking yields work. It could also affect the security of some proof-of-stake networks.
stories.whyItMatters: Staking yields draw many holders to proof-of-stake coins. New EU rules could cut returns or push validators to move elsewhere.
whatToWatch: The outcome of the EU staking review
Any formal rule proposal or timeline from EU regulators
questions: What specific rules will the EU propose?
Which networks and providers would be hit hardest?

sources.title: EU staking review threatens crypto yields and network security could pay the price

stories.title: Stablecoin salaries can cost workers to access their own wages
stories.summary: Some employers now pay wages in stablecoins. CryptoSlate reports that workers can face fees just to convert or withdraw that pay. This adds a hidden cost to a system pitched as cheaper than banks.
stories.whyItMatters: Stablecoin payroll is marketed as a low-cost option for global workers. If fees eat into wages, that pitch weakens.
whatToWatch: Whether providers change fee structures in response
Any regulatory scrutiny of stablecoin payroll fees
questions: Which providers charge these fees, and how much?
Are workers told about the costs before they opt in?

sources.title: Stablecoin salaries can leave workers paying to access their wages

stories.title: Bitcoin's rally past $80,000 lacks institutional backing, CryptoSlate argues
stories.summary: Bitcoin has rallied above $80,000. CryptoSlate argues the move is not driven by strong institutional buying. The piece questions whether the rally can hold without deeper institutional demand.
stories.whyItMatters: A rally without institutional conviction may reverse more sharply, a key concern for readers who track flows rather than price alone.
whatToWatch: Institutional flow data in coming weeks
Whether ETF inflows pick up or stay muted
questions: What data supports the claim of weak institutional conviction?
Could retail-driven demand sustain the rally on its own?

sources.title: Why Bitcoin’s rally above $80,000 isn’t backed by institutional conviction

stories.title: Trump says US will form an 'AI Force' and name an AI czar
stories.summary: President Trump said the US will create an 'AI Force' and appoint a czar to oversee AI policy, according to reports cited by Cointelegraph. Details on scope and timing are not yet clear.
stories.whyItMatters: AI policy shifts can shape the wider regulatory climate crypto shares with the tech sector, though no direct crypto link has been reported yet.
whatToWatch: Official confirmation and details of the AI Force plan
Who is named as AI czar
questions: Does this initiative touch crypto or blockchain policy at all?
What authority would the AI czar role carry?

stories.title: Holding anything but Bitcoin has been a losing bet for two years, Decrypt argues
stories.summary: Decrypt argues that over the past two years, holding other assets instead of Bitcoin has underperformed. The piece is a comparative analysis, not a report of new data or events.
stories.whyItMatters: Comparisons like this feed the ongoing altcoin-versus-Bitcoin debate that shapes portfolio decisions, but framing matters more than the headline claim.
questions: What time frame and assets exactly back this comparison?
Does the analysis account for volatility, not just total return?

sources.title: Why Holding Anything But Bitcoin Has Been a Losing Bet for Two Years

stories.title: Visa moves to close meme coin credit card rewards loophole
stories.summary: Visa is acting to close a loophole that let people earn credit card rewards through meme coin purchases or transactions, Decrypt reports. The move targets how rewards programs interact with crypto spending.
stories.whyItMatters: A payment network tightening crypto-linked reward rules signals growing scrutiny of how crypto plugs into everyday consumer finance.
whatToWatch: When Visa's policy change takes effect
Whether other card networks follow with similar changes
questions: Which specific rewards mechanism was being exploited?
How many users or merchants does this affect?

sources.title: Visa Moves to Close Meme Coin Credit Card Rewards Loophole

stories.title: Grayscale's Zcash ETF files for 3-for-1 forward share split
stories.summary: Grayscale's Zcash ETF has filed for a 3-for-1 forward share split, Cointelegraph reports. A forward split increases the number of shares outstanding and lowers the price per share, without changing the total value held.
stories.whyItMatters: Share splits can make an ETF more accessible to smaller investors and often follow a rise in share price, a sign of demand for the fund.
whatToWatch: Regulatory approval and effective date of the split
Trading volume changes after the split takes effect
questions: What drove the decision to split now?
How has the ETF's share price moved to prompt this?

sources.title: Grayscale’s Zcash ETF files for 3-for-1 forward share split

stories.title: X brings crypto trading closer to your social feed
stories.summary: X is integrating crypto trading features more directly into its platform, CryptoSlate reports. The move puts buying and trading closer to where users already scroll and post.
stories.whyItMatters: A mainstream social platform pushing trading into the feed could widen retail access to crypto, along with the risks of impulsive, feed-driven trades.
whatToWatch: Rollout timeline and which markets or assets are included
Any regulatory response to social-embedded trading
questions: Which exchange or partner powers the trading feature?
What safeguards exist against impulsive trades prompted by social content?

sources.title: X brings crypto trading closer to your social feed

stories.title: Russia's 1% bank crypto cap aims to protect customer assets, CryptoSlate argues
stories.summary: The Bank of Russia has set a strict 1% cap on crypto exposure for banks. CryptoSlate argues the harsh limit is designed to protect bank customers' assets, not just to restrict crypto activity.
stories.whyItMatters: Strict exposure caps show a major regulator treating crypto as a risk to contain within the banking system, a pattern other central banks may watch.
whatToWatch: Whether banks comply within a set timeline
Any adjustment to the cap level over time
questions: Does the cap apply equally to all crypto assets?
How will the Bank of Russia enforce and verify compliance?

sources.title: Why Russia’s harsh 1% crypto cap actually protects bank customer assets

stories.title: Fidelity's $310M surge saves Bitcoin ETFs from a rough week
stories.summary: Fidelity drew in $310 million of Bitcoin ETF inflows, CryptoSlate reports. The surge offset a difficult week for Bitcoin ETFs overall, pulling total flows back into positive territory.
stories.whyItMatters: ETF flow swings give a direct read on institutional demand for Bitcoin, more concrete than price commentary alone.
whatToWatch: Next week's aggregate Bitcoin ETF flow data
Whether other issuers see comparable inflows or keep losing assets
questions: What drove the sudden inflow into Fidelity's fund specifically?
Were other issuers still net negative for the week?

stories.title: Anthropic taps Accenture as embedded evaluator for AI slowdown proposal
stories.summary: Anthropic has brought in Accenture as an embedded evaluator to support a proposal on slowing AI development, Cointelegraph reports. The report does not specify the proposal's full scope.
stories.whyItMatters: AI safety and governance moves from major labs shape the wider tech and regulatory environment, though this story carries no direct crypto angle so far.
whatToWatch: Publication of the full AI slowdown proposal
Accenture's specific role and findings as evaluator
questions: What does the 'AI slowdown proposal' actually call for?
Why does this matter to a crypto-focused reader?

stories.title: Bitcoin's 63% HODL wave isn't the bull signal it looks like, CryptoSlate argues
stories.summary: On-chain data shows 63% of Bitcoin supply has not moved in a long stretch, a pattern known as a HODL wave. CryptoSlate argues this is not the strongly bullish signal many are treating it as.
stories.whyItMatters: On-chain holding metrics get cited often as bullish proof; a skeptical read matters for readers wary of overhyped technical signals.
whatToWatch: How the HODL wave percentage trends in coming weeks
Whether long-term holders begin moving their coins
questions: What time threshold defines 'HODL' in this data?
What alternative explanation does CryptoSlate offer for the wave?

sources.title: Why Bitcoin’s 63% HODL wave isn’t the mega bull signal everyone thinks it is
